the equation of state of isopin-asymmetric nuclear matters in relativistic meanfield models with chiral limit can be consistent with the recent experimental constraints from both heavy-ion reactions and neutron star observations.

we have newly constructed a series of relativistic mean-field equations of state for isospin-asymmetrical nuclear matter with chiral limits, and that they have the special feature that the symmetry energy at intermediate densities is soft but stiff at high density, and the resulting neutron star properties are consistent with the recent observations.

the Brown–Rha scaling of the in-medium hadron masses and the natural choice of the coupling constants in the relativistic mean-field approach can lead to the equation of state that is soft at sub-satuation densities and stiff at supra-normal densities, consistent with the recent experimental data from heavy-ion reactions, and that such equation of state can lead to a canonical mass neutron star and a maximum neutron star mass close to the recent observation.

the Brown–Rhp scaling is not necessary for a realistic equation of state of isosymmetric nuclear matter at high densities, and that the Brown–Rh scaling is only needed to soften the equation of state of nuclear matter at high isospin asymmetry.

the chiral symmetry plays an important role in determining the equation of state of isobaric asymmetric nuclear matter at supra-normal densities.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the equation of state of isobaric nuclear matter at supra-normal densities can be constrained by the collective flow and isospin diffusion observables from high energy heavy ion reactions, which can be further tested by the upcoming heavy-ion reaction experiments at the Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research (FAIR) and the Nuclotron-based Ion Collider fAcility (NICA).

the Brown–Rha scaling and the chiral symmetry breaking at supra-normal density can naturally lead to a softening of the equation of state at intermediate densities and a stiffening of the equation state at high densities.

the Brown–Rha scaling can be used as an effective tool to soften the equation of state at intermediate densities, while the naturalness of the parameters can be employed to stiffen the equation of state of neutron-rich nuclear matter at high densities, leading to a soft equation of state at low and intermediate densities, but a stiff equation of state at high densities.
